doc.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024

title: Drummers behind bass solos; Rufus Reid
summary: Responding to Neal Caine's quote, Soph says to treat bass solos like horn solos, a lesson from Rufus Reid.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Along those same lines, I’m going to read a quote here from a bass player named Neal Caine, who is a fairly young man, I think he’s from New Orleans, a marvelous player who played here. And he was addressing the issue — I think I asked him about bass solos.

And he says, “When you think about the fact that we spend our whole careers making everyone else sound good on their solos and then we get our solo and the drummer goes to the hi-hat and the piano player just sits there. It’s infuriating to me.”

And I wanted to ask him what he liked but, so if there’s a question here, if you’re on a date, especially where it’s one of those dates like meet the group on the bandstand, hi how are you doing, and it comes time for a bass solo, what’s your inclination to do?

Well if it’s appropriate stylistically — I’ll just put it this way — if it’s a swing gig, Benny Goodman sort of music, Basie kind of music, straight ahead 4/4, more than likely the bass player is going to expect you to go to the hi-hat.

Yeah. But I learned, Rufus Reid and I have played off and on together for years. It’s got to be close to 40 years now that we’ve known each other. And the first time I played with Rufus — because when you first meet him he’s a pretty intimidating guy. A big guy with a low voice who speaks slowly. Look out. And I went to the hi-hat behind his solo. And he looked at me and man it was like Mount Vesuvius had erupted. He says, “Don’t do that, treat me like a horn player dammit.” And that was it. Back to the ride cymbal, comping, the whole thing only on another dynamic level of course. So and to this day
there are still times when I’ll approach the bass solo like that but the bass player will say, “Hey man, I’d really like it if you’d just go to the hi-hat.” So again —
